transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: —and I think we can keep this pretty lean since we only have ten minutes. Um, before we get into it, I've got the district's March 15 registration export penciled in, which is kind of the hinge for the whole six-week schedule. What I'm hoping we can settle today is how much we trust that matching approach for picking the first clinic sites, and whether Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge still make sense for those late-March evening clinics.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: —Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge still make sense as the first sites, yes. Coverage is low, there are enough incoming children that it’s not just a small-denominator effect, and that’s where we saw transmission. I’d use the March 15 export for siting, but I’m less comfortable using it as a complete invitation list. The Cedar Grove registry match had more unmatched records than I expected. Marcus, can the address export be refreshed weekly once registration opens, or—

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: The district says they can refresh it weekly once registration opens, so I can use each export to update the map and the outreach queue. The unmatched Cedar Grove records are a reason not to make it invitation-only, though. We should keep the clinics open and use school channels broadly. Lena, for location, if the individual addresses are messy, is the match quality still good enough at the catchment level?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: At the catchment level, yes, I think it’s good enough for that first decision. The unmatched records could shift the exact child count, but they’re not enough to erase the pattern. Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge are low on both coverage and volume. I’d just want to rerun the match after the registry cleanup before we start- before we describe neighborhood-level gaps too precisely.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: That gives me enough to hold Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge for the first two evening sites. But let's keep the language broad and not say we've identified specific blocks. Aisha, before we move on, if families get an appointment message based on the registration file, does that usually feel useful, or can it come across as surveillance-y, especially with the measles situation?

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: It can be useful if it comes across as an offer, not as evidence the district has flagged them. I’d avoid individualized language about status, and make it really plain whether it’s a reminder, a requirement, or just help booking. Parents were genuinely unclear about that in the listening sessions. Could the link invite questions or, um, barriers as well as appointments?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: Yeah, I think we can do that. The link could have two paths, one to book a slot and one to tell us what would make it workable, like hours, transportation, language, that kind of thing, without asking people to explain their vaccination status. I’m still puzzled by the weak evening response last winter, so that feedback might tell us whether these late-March sites actually fit families’ schedules.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: And I'd make that second path feel like a real response channel, not just a form that disappears. Even a short option like, "I have a question about what the school requires," could matter, because that confusion came up a lot. Do we know whether a parent liaison could see the themes coming in without seeing identifiable family information, or—

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: I think so, but I need to check what the district will allow the liaison to receive. We could give them a weekly de-identified themes sheet with questions about requirements, hours, rides, language, that kind of thing, and use that to adjust the final-week-of-March Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge clinics without turning it into a case-management inbox.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That would be useful, especially if the themes sheet tells us whether we're simply not reaching families who haven't registered yet. Aisha, in your local work, what channels have actually reached those parents before they show up in the school file? I'm worried the weekly exports will get better, but still- they'll leave out the group we most need to find.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: Um, parent liaisons are probably the strongest route, especially through preschool programs, WIC, and the informal parent networks around the elementary schools. Faith communities may reach some families too, but I'd need to check who's willing on this timeline before we promise that. Could the broad school message point families to a liaison or a, um, neutral county contact, so people who aren't yet in the registration file have somewhere to start?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: A neutral county contact is better. We don't want the school file to feel like the gatekeeper. We can put the clinic schedule and a simple call or text option in the broad message, then have liaisons and WIC or preschool partners share the same thing. I just need to check whether our call line can handle questions in the main languages. We can't advertise that, that piece and then strand people.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: And if the line can’t reliably answer in the main languages, I’d keep the broad message to the concrete basics and route language-specific questions through partners we know can help. Could you check what the actual coverage is before we name the text option? A bad first contact would travel fast through those parent networks, and—

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: I’ll check the call-line language coverage and whether we can staff a text response before we put either one in the message. For late March, I’d keep the broad outreach to the clinic dates, walk-in availability, and a county contact we know works, rather than overpromise. Then we can add the tailored booking link to the weekly registration outreach once that’s ready.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Mm, yeah, that's important.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: And just so we don't let the booking link become the whole strategy, the broad message should say clearly that the clinics are open to families whether or not they've registered yet. I think that matters practically, and because it avoids making school enrollment feel like a, um, monitoring threshold.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: I'll make that explicit. The clinics are open to any family with a school-entry vaccine need, registered or not. Since we're tight on time, I need to confirm staffing and vaccine order before I put a capacity number on Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge. I'd rather publish walk-in hours than appointment slots we can't actually absorb.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That’s probably the right call. For the first two sites, open walk-in hours give us a cleaner read on demand than just filling the families already visible in registration. Though I’d want us to count registrations versus walk-ins, if we can, just to see who the school file is...

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: We can capture that at check-in, whether they came through registration outreach, a partner, or just walked in, without making it a big intake burden. I'll make sure the paper or tablet flow has that, and then we can compare it after the first site. If most people are walk-ins, that changes how hard we- how hard we lean on the weekly match.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: And could we add just one nonidentifying field for catchment, if the address is available at check-in? I don't need exact addresses, just whether walk-ins are coming from Cedar Grove and Maple Ridge versus elsewhere. That would help us see whether the sites are reaching the areas we intended, or whether we need to, um, relocate the later clinics.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: We can add catchment at check-in and keep it optional if someone doesn't want to give an address. I'll make it a simple dropdown, Cedar Grove, Maple Ridge, other, or, um, unknown, plus the referral source. Then we can see whether the first two sites are actually drawing from those areas before we commit to the later locations.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: I like making it optional. I’d also be careful that “referral source” includes something like parent liaison, preschool/WIC, faith partner, and “heard from another parent,” rather than putting all of that, all of that into other. We’ll learn a lot about which relationships are actually carrying the invitation.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: We can build that in. We’ll keep those as separate check-in choices, plus school message and walk-in, so we don’t lose the partner signal. I’m a little wary of making the form too long at a busy evening clinic, but those are probably the few fields— actually, the fields worth protecting.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Yeah, those seem like the right few fields to protect.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: Mm, that’s a manageable set.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: I’ll keep it to those fields and pilot the flow at Cedar Grove instead of trying to perfect it on paper. I need to check the staffing and language coverage today, because that’s what determines whether those walk-in hours are actually usable. But the siting and the basic intake approach- those feel settled enough for me to keep moving.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Okay, I think we should stop there—the rest can, uh, wait until next time. Thanks, both.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Aisha Bell
transcript.text: All right, take care—bye.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Chen
transcript.text: Sounds good—talk soon.
